o: Paul expresses great affection for Timothy.
Exhorts him to improve his spiritual gifts.
Tells of many who basely deserted him; but speaks with affection of Onesiphorus.
bg: timothy, second epistle to

Was probably written a year or so after the first, and from Rome, where Paul was for a second time a prisoner, and was sent to Timothy by the hands of Tychicus. In it he entreats Timothy to come to him before winter, and to bring Mark with him (comp. Phil. 2:22).
Hold
A fortress, the name given to David's lurking-places (1 Sam. 22:4, 5; 24:22).
Asia

(orient). The passages in the New Testament where this word occurs are the following; (Acts 2:9; 6:9; 16:6; 19:10,22,26,27; 20:4,16,18; 21:27; 27:2; Romans 16:5; 1 Corinthians 16:19; 2 Corinthians 1:8; 2 Timothy 1:15; 1 Peter 1:1; Revelation 1:4,11) In all these it may be confidently stated that the word is used for a Roman province which embraced the western part of the peninsula of Asia Minor and of which Ephesus w
Ephesus

Two of Paul's companions, Trophimus and Tychicus, were probably natives of Ephesus (Acts 20:4; 21:29; 2 Tim. 4:12). In his second epistle to Timothy, Paul speaks of Onesiphorus as having served him in many things at Ephesus (2 Tim. 1:18).
ch.s: This chapter covers: Paul expresses great affection for Timothy (vv. 1–5); Exhorts him to improve his spiritual gifts (vv. 6–14); Tells of many who basely deserted him; but speaks with affection of Onesiphorus (vv. 15–18). People named: Paul, Lois, Eunice, Phygellus, Hermogenes, Onesiphorus. Places: Hold, Asia, Ephesus.
ch.mh: The promise of eternal life to believers in Christ Jesus, is the leading subject of ministers who are employed according to the will of God.
q: Read verses 1–5 (Paul expresses great affection for Timothy). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 6–14 (Exhorts him to improve his spiritual gifts), what do you learn about grace and mercy?
Verse 7 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Romans 8:15. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Paul’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of faith and trust in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Timothy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And if we would have mercy then, we must seek for it now of the Lord.
ch.a: Show the same mercy you have received to someone who does not deserve it.

o: The apostle exhorts Timothy to persevere with diligence, like a soldier, a combatant, and a husbandman.
Encouraging him by assurances of a happy end of his faithfulness.
Warnings to shun vain babblings and dangerous errors.
Charges to flee youthful lusts, and to minister with zeal against error, but with meekness of spirit.
bg: timothy, second epistle to

Was probably written a year or so after the first, and from Rome, where Paul was for a second time a prisoner, and was sent to Timothy by the hands of Tychicus. In it he entreats Timothy to come to him before winter, and to bring Mark with him (comp. Phil. 2:22).
Philetus
Amiable, with Hymenaeus, at Ephesus, said that the "resurrection was past already" (2 Tim. 2:17, 18). This was a Gnostic heresy held by the Nicolaitanes.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle exhorts Timothy to persevere with diligence, like a soldier, a combatant, and a husbandman (vv. 1–7); Encouraging him by assurances of a happy end of his faithfulness (vv. 8–13); Warnings to shun vain babblings and dangerous errors (vv. 14–21); Charges to flee youthful lusts, and to minister with zeal against error, but with meekness of spirit (vv. 22–26). People named: David, Hymeneus, Philetus. Places: No.
ch.mh: As our trials increase, we need to grow stronger in that which is good; our faith stronger, our resolution stronger, our love to God and Christ stronger.
q: Read verses 1–7 (The apostle exhorts Timothy to persevere with diligence, like a soldier, a combatant, and a husbandman). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 8–13 (Encouraging him by assurances of a happy end of his faithfulness), what do you learn about faith and trust?
Verse 19 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside John 10:14. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does David’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of suffering and endurance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Timothy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: And if any long for deliverance, let them remember they never can escape, except by repentance, which is the gift of God; and we must ask it of him by earnest, persevering prayer.
ch.a: Name one worry and deliberately hand it over to God in prayer each day this week.

o: The apostle foretells the rise of dangerous enemies to the gospel.
Proposes his own example to Timothy.
And exhorts him to continue in the doctrine he had learned from the Holy Scriptures.
bg: timothy, second epistle to

Was probably written a year or so after the first, and from Rome, where Paul was for a second time a prisoner, and was sent to Timothy by the hands of Tychicus. In it he entreats Timothy to come to him before winter, and to bring Mark with him (comp. Phil. 2:22).
Antioch
IN Syria. The capital of the Greek kings of Syria, and afterwards the residence of the Roman governors of the province which bore the same name.
Iconium
The capital of ancient Lycaonia. It was first visited by Paul and Barnabas from Antioch-in-Pisidia during the apostle's first missionary journey (Acts 13:50, 51).
Lystra
A town of Lycaonia, in Asia Minor, in a wild district and among a rude population. Here Paul preached the gospel after he had been driven by persecution from Iconium (Acts 14:2-7).
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle foretells the rise of dangerous enemies to the gospel (vv. 1–9); Proposes his own example to Timothy (vv. 10–13); And exhorts him to continue in the doctrine he had learned from the Holy Scriptures (vv. 14–17). People named: Jambres, Moses. Places: Antioch, Iconium, Lystra.
ch.mh: Even in gospel times there would be perilous times; on account of persecution from without, still more on account of corruptions within.
q: Read verses 1–9 (The apostle foretells the rise of dangerous enemies to the gospel). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 10–13 (Proposes his own example to Timothy), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 16 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Romans 15:4. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Jambres’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of faith and trust in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Timothy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Oh that we may love our Bibles more, and keep closer to them! then shall we find benefit, and at last gain the happiness therein promised by faith in our Lord Jesus Christ, who is the main subject of both Testaments.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.

o: The apostle solemnly charges Timothy to be diligent, though many will not bear sound doctrine.
Enforces the charge from his own martyrdom, then at hand.
He cautions, and complains of such as had deserted him; and expresses his faith as to his own preservation to the heavenly kingdom.
Friendly greetings and his usual blessing.
bg: timothy, second epistle to

Was probably written a year or so after the first, and from Rome, where Paul was for a second time a prisoner, and was sent to Timothy by the hands of Tychicus. In it he entreats Timothy to come to him before winter, and to bring Mark with him (comp. Phil. 2:22).
Thessalonica
A large and populous city on the Thermaic bay. It was the capital of one of the four Roman districts of Macedonia, and was ruled by a praetor.
Galatia

During his second missionary journey Paul, accompanied by Silas and Timothy (Acts 16:6), visited the "region of Galatia," where he was detained by sickness (Gal. 4:13), and had thus the longer opportunity of preaching to them the gospel. On his third journey he went over "all the country of Galatia and Phrygia in order" (Acts 18:23).
Dalmatia
A mountainous country on the eastern shore of the Adriatic, a part of the Roman province of Illyricum. It still bears its ancient name.
ch.s: This chapter covers: The apostle solemnly charges Timothy to be diligent, though many will not bear sound doctrine (vv. 1–5); Enforces the charge from his own martyrdom, then at hand (vv. 6–8); Desires him to come speedily (vv. 9–13); He cautions, and complains of such as had deserted him; and expresses his faith as to his own preservation to the heavenly kingdom (vv. 14–18); Friendly greetings and his usual blessing (vv. 19–22). People named: Demas, Crescens, Titus, Luke, Mark, Tychicus. Places: Thessalonica, Galatia, Dalmatia, Ephesus, Troas.
ch.mh: People will turn away from the truth, they will grow weary of the plain gospel of Christ, they will be greedy of fables, and take pleasure in them.
q: Read verses 1–5 (The apostle solemnly charges Timothy to be diligent, though many will not bear sound doctrine). What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 6–8 (Enforces the charge from his own martyrdom, then at hand), what do you learn about suffering and endurance?
Verse 18 is one of the most cross-referenced verses in this chapter. Read it alongside Psalms 121:7. How do the two passages shed light on each other?
What does Demas’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of salvation and redemption in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 2 Timothy?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.aq: Let us thank the Divine goodness in having given us so many writings of wise and pious men in all ages; and let us seek that by reading them our profiting may appear to all.
ch.a: Bring a present hardship to God and memorize the key verse as an anchor.
